statement: What value of $x$ satisfies the equation $3(x - 4) + 2 = 5x - 18$?

choices.misconception: I got to $-2x = -8$ and then divided as if the signs were different, so I wrote $x = -4$.
I multiplied the 3 by the $x$ but not by the $-4$, so I had $3x - 4 + 2 = 5x - 18$ and got $x = 8$.
I moved the $-10$ across the equals sign but left it as $-10$, so I got $-2x = -28$ and $x = 14$.

hints: Start by distributing the $3$ to both terms inside the parentheses.
After distributing, combine like terms on the left, then gather the $x$ terms on one side and the numbers on the other.
The left side becomes $3x - 12 + 2 = 3x - 10$, so $3x - 10 = 5x - 18$. Subtract $3x$ and add $18$ to both sides.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
